name: CapCut Player 3 Smooth Caption Compounds
use_when: A social edit needs smooth animated captions that feel more polished than default auto captions.
The captions can be split into short phrase groups and compounded before styling.
The text effect is meant to support a premium social look without becoming the main visual focus.
avoid_when: Auto-caption wording, timing, line breaks, or placement have not been corrected.
The captions are accessibility-critical and need stable plain subtitles.
The background is too busy or bright for the Player 3 effect to preserve readable text edges.
Faces, product UI, proof, or other designed text already occupy the caption region.

timeline_pattern.pattern: auto_captions -> correct_text_and_line_splits -> compound_each_caption_group -> align_compounds -> apply_player_3_effect -> set_texture_to_0 -> paste_attributes_to_remaining_compounds -> phone_size_qc
timeline_pattern.line_split_rule: Split captions into phrase-readable groups before compounding; small stacks such as 3 words, then 2 words, then 2 words can work when the meaning remains clear.
timeline_pattern.compound_rule: Compound each caption group so the video effect can be applied consistently to the group instead of to loose caption fragments.
timeline_pattern.attribute_rule: Paste attributes to the remaining caption compounds only after the first compound passes readability, timing, and contrast review.

motion.rule: The effect should feel smooth and integrated while settling before the spoken phrase needs to be read.

keyframe_values.texture: Set Player 3 Texture to 0 as a clean starting point, then adjust only if readability improves.
keyframe_values.clip_length: Trim each compound to the spoken phrase; do not let the effect linger into the next caption.
keyframe_values.paste_attributes: Apply the same effect to matching caption groups, then review each phrase because the same effect can fail on a different background.

sound.rule: No SFX is required; speech clarity and caption readability are more important than decorating continuous captions.

captions.rule: Treat auto captions as draft text until spelling, timing, phrase splits, safe placement, and duplicate visual-text conflicts are fixed.

color.rule: The caption effect must remain readable on the actual footage, including bright, dark, busy, and face-heavy frames.

implementation.ffmpeg: Approximate with ASS subtitles or short drawtext groups plus subtle alpha/fontsize/blur envelopes only when readable; use contact sheets for every caption region.
implementation.remotion: Represent each caption group as a Sequence-local component with phraseLines, effectType: player3_smooth, texture: 0, safeRegion, startFrame, endFrame, spring or fade settings, and contrastQcStatus.
implementation.blender: Use text objects or compositor text groups with restrained material/opacity motion only for controlled renders; keep accessibility subtitles separate.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Generate auto captions, correct and split lines, compound each caption group, place compounds cleanly on the timeline, apply Effects > Player 3 to one compound, set Texture to 0, paste attributes to matching compounds, then inspect every phrase at phone size.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Correct captions first, upgrade selected groups to graphics or nests, apply a subtle tested text animation/blur preset, then review collisions and contrast against the final footage.

common_mistakes: Compounding captions before correcting the auto-caption text.
Pasting Player 3 attributes across all captions without checking each background.
Using the effect on long subtitles that need stable accessibility-first reading.
Leaving caption groups scattered across tracks so timing and cleanup become messy.
Letting the animation run under the next phrase or another designed text layer.
qc: Are auto-caption words, timing, phrase splits, and placement corrected before compounding?
Does every Player 3 caption group remain readable at phone size?
Does the effect settle before the phrase needs to be read?
Do captions avoid faces, proof, product UI, and designed text?
Were pasted attributes reviewed on every affected caption group?
